description:
The National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) is a welfare initiative by the Government of India. 

It aims to provide financial assistance to families in the event of the death of the primary breadwinner. 

The objective is to alleviate the financial burden on families during times of crisis. 

Under the scheme, a one-time financial assistance of Rs. 20,000 is provided to the bereaved family. 

This assistance is intended to help families cope with immediate expenses after the loss of the breadwinner. 

Eligibility for the scheme includes families belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) categories. 

The primary breadwinner must be aged between 18 to 59 years at the time of death. 

The application process involves submitting a death certificate of the breadwinner along with proof of BPL status. 

Applications can be made through the local government offices or designated agencies. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Rural Development at the state level. 

The assistance is provided as a one-time payment and does not have a recurring timeline. 

The scheme is operational across all states and Union Territories in India. 

It is part of the broader social security initiatives aimed at supporting vulnerable families.
